. Post
hoc review of clinical trials suggests that B-vitamin supplementation and homocysteine-lowering may be particularly beneﬁcial
for prevention of stroke and the slowing of cognitive decline and brain atrophy in older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
Additional randomized control trials are needed to provide more deﬁnitive answers.
